project.name: ImgLab
project.context: Goal-first public image processing workbench with optional backend processing.
project.domain: Browser-based public image inspection and export workbench
project.runtimeConstraint: React + Vite + Tailwind CSS + DaisyUI frontend, FastAPI backend for processing.
project.architectureConstraint: Client-side SPA with optional API backend for heavy processing.

assumptions: Frontend uses /api endpoints for processing when backend is available.
UI must avoid grid or glow wallpaper and keep image color judgment intact.
Design contract follows the light inspection studio anchor.
MVP is complete; current UI must read as a production public product.
motionPaletteDecision: Motion: comparison wipe reveal with a physical handle and reduced-motion fade fallback. Palette: light studio shell, warm paper panels, graphite text, blue primary actions, and cool cyan measurement accents.

conceptualAnchor.name: Light inspection studio
conceptualAnchor.anchorReference: public image inspection studio with calibrated review table, neutral paper panels, focused image stage, measurement controls, and export tray
conceptualAnchor.specificReferencePoint: A bright review table where the image sits in a controlled stage, goals are arranged as inspection choices, and export formats sit in a final output tray.
conceptualAnchor.rationale: Anchors the UI in a credible public product workflow without the heaviness of a darkroom interface or decorative wallpaper patterns.
conceptualAnchor.signatureMotion: A comparison wipe reveals processed pixels over the original image.
conceptualAnchor.signatureMove: A physical handle sits on the wipe line and can be dragged by the user.
conceptualAnchor.typographicDecision: Compact operation titles, plain body copy, small metadata labels, aligned numeric parameter and output format values.

visualResetStrategy: Shift the previous dark bench composition into a light public inspection studio with bright shell surfaces, a dark neutral image stage, stronger first-viewport hierarchy, production copy, explicit export tray, and no coursework or MVP framing.

derivedTokenLogic.anchorReference: public image inspection studio with calibrated review table, neutral paper panels, focused image stage, measurement controls, and export tray
derivedTokenLogic.colorDerivationSource: Studio white shell, warm paper panels, graphite labels, blue action controls, and cool cyan measurement cues.
derivedTokenLogic.spacingDerivationSource: Inspection studio table with clear stage separation, compact tool grouping, and attached export controls.
derivedTokenLogic.typographyDerivationSource: Technical labeling from inspection equipment: compact titles, small metadata, monospaced output details.
derivedTokenLogic.motionDerivationSource: Manual comparison wipe, decisive status shifts, and short fades for state changes.
derivedTokenLogic.validationRule: Every token must trace to the light studio anchor; no grid or glow wallpaper tokens are allowed.

functionalRoles: inspection blue indicates primary actions and export readiness
cyan indicates measurement, focus, and wipe handle
format controls use paper surfaces with blue selected states
colorTruth.nonTransferableBehavior: A bright studio shell paired with a dark neutral image stage is specific to image inspection because the surrounding UI stays public and readable while the image area preserves contrast judgment.

crossViewportAdaptation.mobile: Upload or stage first, goal rail follows, export tray stays directly under processed result.
crossViewportAdaptation.tablet: Stage and goal rail split into two columns; export controls remain attached to status metadata.
crossViewportAdaptation.desktop: Stage dominates left; goal rail is a vertical contact sheet on the right with a persistent export tray.

motionSystem.reducedMotionFallback: Immediate swap or short fade with no wipe animation.

componentMorphology.stage: Focused dark-neutral image stage with a wipe line and handle.
componentMorphology.goalRail: Compact stacked buttons with intent summary.
componentMorphology.statusPill: Service indicator with backend readiness label.
componentMorphology.dropzone: Framed pad with dashed edge and clear action copy.
componentMorphology.exportTray: Segmented output format controls and a single decisive export button.

aiSafeUiAudit.failureDefinition: Fails if grid, line, or glow wallpaper appears or if calibration marks become page background.
aiSafeUiAudit.backgroundPatternRule: No decorative grid, scanlines, or radial glow backgrounds.

productionContentPolicy.rule: Goal copy must describe user intent and match real operations. Product UI must not use homework, demo, MVP, placeholder, or scaffold language.

accessibilityPolicy.focusVisibility: Visible focus ring on all interactive elements.
accessibilityPolicy.keyboardAccess: Goal list and wipe slider must be keyboard operable.

implementationOrder: Finalize goal rail, status pill, and export format tray
designExecutionHandoff.notes: Keep backgrounds clean and avoid decorative lines or glows.

mustPass: Export choices include PNG, JPEG, and WebP where browser support exists
Focus and contrast meet WCAG 2.2 AA
driftSignals: Goal rail looks like a default card list
Export feels like an afterthought or single-format MVP artifact
Calibration marks appear in the background

allowedSources: official React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, DaisyUI docs

libraryDecisions.purpose: Component model for the frontend UI.
libraryDecisions.fallback: Use the existing static HTML build if React tooling fails.

libraryDecisions.purpose: Frontend dev server and build tool.
libraryDecisions.fallback: Use the static server for local-only preview.

libraryDecisions.purpose: Utility styling and token mapping via DaisyUI.
libraryDecisions.fallback: Use scoped CSS for critical layout if Tailwind config fails.

libraryDecisions.purpose: Semantic component styling and theme tokens.
libraryDecisions.fallback: Swap to base Tailwind utility styling.

repoEvidence.designEvidenceSummary: Frontend exists under frontend/ with React + Vite + Tailwind + DaisyUI. Current UI uses goal-first buttons, backend /api processing, comparison wipe, and export format choices. The current design direction is light inspection studio.
